slides.title: Defining Problem Statements
text: Defining Problem Statements
FIT1055 IT Professional Practice and Ethics | Monash University

The integrated sources will be further analyzed to develop strong problem statements. A problem statement is a clear, concise description of an issue or challenge that needs to be addressed. It defines how the system should ideally behave, what the problem is, why it matters, who it affects, what issues may arise after implementation, and what the desired outcome should be. Think of it as the foundation that guides your entire research or project—it tells you exactly what you're trying to solve.

slides.title: Defining Problem Statements
text: Defining Problem Statements
The How–What–Why Framework
FIT1055 IT Professional Practice and Ethics | Monash University
A strong problem statement in AI ethics requires moving from scattered information to structured analysis.
How
How should AI systems operate under ideal conditions?
What
What are the specific ethical issues that arose from the real-world AI deployment?
Why
Why did these ethical issues arise from the AI implementation? What is the root cause?
A pattern is a high-level concept you define based on recurring themes/incidents highlighted from your sources.

slides.title: Identify the Patterns from Integrated Sources – the "How"
text: Identify the Patterns from Integrated Sources – the "How"
Therefore, we can define the following.
FIT1055 IT Professional Practice and Ethics | Monash University
How AI Should Work Ideally in Healthcare — Seamless Integration Model
Workflow Enhancement, Not Replacement:
AI should integrate directly into existing Electronic Health Records (EHR) systems without requiring separate applications
Healthcare professionals should interact with AI through familiar interfaces, not learn entirely new systems
AI assistance should appear contextually when needed, rather than requiring active invocation

slides.title: Identify the Patterns from Integrated Sources – the "What"
text: Identify the Patterns from Integrated Sources – the "What"
Identify the patterns to identify "What" are the ethical issues that arose from the real-world AI deployment
FIT1055 IT Professional Practice and Ethics | Monash University
Pattern 1: Accuracy and Reliability
Issue: Hallucinations and misinformation in critical medical contexts
Examples: Generating plausible but incorrect drug interactions, dosages, or treatment protocols
Risk: Patient harm from following AI-generated medical advice
Pattern 2: Bias and Discrimination
Issue: Perpetuating existing healthcare disparities
Examples: Different treatment recommendations based on patient demographics; underrepresenting certain populations in training data
Risk: Amplifying racial, gender, or socioeconomic biases in medical care

slides.title: Identify the Patterns from Integrated Sources – the "Why"
text: Identify the Patterns from Integrated Sources – the "Why"
Identify the patterns to identify "Why" these ethical issues arise from the AI implementation? What is the root cause?
FIT1055 IT Professional Practice and Ethics | Monash University
Pattern 1: Dehumanization Through Algorithmic Reductionism

Root Cause: AI systems process patients as statistical data points rather than recognizing their complexity as human beings Mechanism: Algorithms reduce multifaceted medical decisions to mathematical calculations, losing the nuanced understanding that human judgment provides

slides.title: Identify the Patterns from Integrated Sources – the "Why"
text: Identify the Patterns from Integrated Sources – the "Why"
Identify the patterns to identify "Why" did these ethical issues arise from the AI implementation? What is the root cause?
FIT1055 IT Professional Practice and Ethics | Monash University
Pattern 2: Erosion of Patient Autonomy

Root Cause: AI systems make or heavily influence medical decisions without adequate patient involvement or informed consent Mechanism: Automated recommendations may bypass patient consultation, or patients may not understand how AI influences their care options

How-What-Why Integration Analysis — How AI Should Ideally Function vs. Current Reality

The Integration Gap: Current patterns show AI being adopted primarily for administrative efficiency (documentation, summarization, data interpretation), but ideal implementation requires a human-centric collaborative framework.

slides.title: From Pattern Analysis to Define Problem Statement
text: From Pattern Analysis to Define Problem Statement
How, What, Why → a synthesis of new understanding
FIT1055 IT Professional Practice and Ethics | Monash University
A human-centric collaborative framework is where:
Seamless workflow integration replaces the current fragmented, application-switching approach
Contextual intelligence emerges naturally within clinical workflows rather than requiring separate AI consultations
Professional enhancement occurs without compromising clinical judgment development
Patient-centered outcomes drive system design rather than administrative convenience

New Insight: The efficiency gains healthcare workers seek through AI adoption inadvertently create systemic vulnerabilities when the technology is not designed with ethical principles as foundational requirements rather than add-on considerations.
